title: Thresholded shadow + binary-split rollout and rollback playbook for pinned model variants
creator: Priya Nair
description: Define and deliver a tested canary/A-B rollout strategy for new model versions behind customer pins that combines: (1) a thresholded shadowing phase for quality signal collection without customer-facing risk, (2) a controlled binary-split phase for real traffic validation with hard SLO gates, and (3) an automated rollback/playbook that triggers on latency/quality/cost regressions. This work ties into the model onboarding flow and the published performance profile so customers using pinned variants can safely upgrade with measurable risk and predictable economics.
acceptance_criteria: A documented two-stage rollout pattern (shadow -> binary split) for pinned model variants published in the Console runbooks
Shadowing collects representative quality signals (sampled prompts, embeddings similarity, hallucination rate) and latency/cost telemetry per-customer and per-route
Binary-split rollout automation can be parameterized by: initial split %, per-minute ramp, max latency delta, quality regression thresholds, and cost threshold
Automatic rollback executes within configured SLAs when any gate trips and creates a post-rollback incident summary with telemetry links
E2E tests (simulated traffic) validate gating behavior for latency spike, quality regression, and cost anomaly scenarios
Docs and a short tutorial in Console show how to run a pinned-model upgrade using the new playbook and how to interpret published performance profile changes
notes: Rationale: Many enterprise customers pin model revisions for deterministic behavior. A naive canary risks data quality/regression and exposes customers to latency/cost surprises. Shadowing alone doesn’t validate runtime interactions under load. Combining both reduces blast radius and provides an auditable path for upgrades.

Trade-offs considered: Full progressive traffic splitting by micro-cohorts is powerful but complex (requires cohort management and billing changes) => chosen approach targets 90% of use cases while keeping console UX simple.

Metrics we'll measure: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, per-request token cost, response-length-normalized cost, model quality delta on golden prompts (ROUGE/EMB-sim/hallucination heuristics), end-user visible error rate, and rollback frequency.

Telemetry links (placeholders): Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PM-15678+rollout+playbook, Grafana dashboard proto: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pinned-rollouts, GitHub PR w/ automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7281.

Rollout knobs to expose in Console: shadow sampling rate, allowed quality delta (absolute and relative), allowed latency delta (ms and percent), initial split percent, ramp schedule (linear/minute), emergency cutoff threshold, and whether rollback is automatic or manual.

Privacy note: Shadowing will route copies of requests only for customers who opt-in to upgrade trials or for internal staging customers. We must ensure PII redaction hooks are applied before shadow copies leave customer VPCs. Security team flagged this as a follow-up (see ENG-4279).

implementation_notes: Phase 1 (shadow-only): implement non-blocking shadow route that tags requests and writes to a shadow telemetry index. Aggregation job computes quality deltas using baseline golden prompt set and per-customer prompt samples.
Phase 2 (binary split): implement routing logic in control plane to split traffic at route level with ramping. Use existing rollout infra where possible; fallback to pinned baseline if gate trips.

Phase 3 (automation & playbook): author runbook steps for operators including: pre-checks, enabling shadow, waiting window, promoting split, monitoring gates, and executing rollback. Automate rollback trigger with hooks into incident manager.
Testing: synthetic load tests, fault injection (slow kernel, memory pressure), and quality regression injection (altered model weights) to validate gate behavior.
Docs: publish a Console tutorial, API spec for upgrade endpoints, and a short FAQ for customers explaining guarantees and expected metrics during rollouts.
